2607.06101.title: Agents That Teach: Towards Designing Incidental Learning Back into AI-Assisted Software Development
2607.06101.paper_summary: AI coding agents are rapidly reshaping how software is built, with developers increasingly delegating substantial coding tasks to autonomous agents in pursuit of higher productivity. While these gains are real, they come at the cost of incidental learning. Developers historically acquired informal knowledge through effortful problem-solving, and this has long shaped how software engineering expertise develops. However, with over-reliance on agentic coding, unpracticed skills could atrophy silently over time. As this learning pathway is short-circuited, developers risk silently accruing Knowledge Debt, a developer-level analogue of Technical Debt, where changes the agent executes that the developer cannot fully understand accrue over time. In this paper, we argue that incidental learning will not re-emerge on its own and must be consciously designed back into developer-agent interactions, and propose six design principles to guide such systems. We then present "SHIELD", a multi-agent system grounded in the notion of "agents that teach", that operationalizes these principles by leveraging the AI coding agent's own reasoning to surface contextual, out-of-band learning moments without disrupting developer flow. Through this work, we envision a path toward learning-aware development environments where productivity and learning are complementary, not competing.
2607.06101.paper_summary_zh: AI 編碼代理正在迅速改變軟體的建構方式，開發者越來越多地將大量編碼任務委託給自主代理，以追求更高的生產力。<lb/>雖然這些增益是真實的，但卻以偶然學習為代價。<lb/>開發者歷來透過艱苦的問題解決獲得非正式知識，這長期以來塑造了軟體工程專業知識的發展。<lb/>然而，隨著對代理編碼的過度依賴，未經練習的技能可能會隨著時間的推移而默默萎縮。<lb/>隨著這一學習途徑被短路，開發者面臨著默默積累知識債務的風險，這是開發者層面的技術債務類比，代理執行的變更開發者無法完全理解，隨著時間的推移而累積。<lb/>在本文中，我們主張偶然學習不會自動重新出現，必須在開發者與代理的互動中有意識地重新設計進去，並提出六項設計原則來指導這樣的系統。<lb/>然後，我們介紹了 "SHIELD"，一個基於 "教學代理" 概念的多代理系統，通過利用 AI 編碼代理自身的推理來實現這些原則，從而在不打斷開發者工作流程的情況下，顯現出上下文的、非正式的學習時刻。<lb/>通過這項工作，我們展望了一條通向學習意識開發環境的道路，在這裡生產力和學習是互補的，而不是競爭的。
